class.name: BulletPickupData2D
class.brief_description: What a bullet becomes when it is turned into a pickup: coin, gem, score item.
class.description:
Describes a pickup for [method BulletFactory2D.convert_all_bullets_to_pickups], [method BulletFactory2D.convert_bullets_in_circle_to_pickups], [method BulletFactory2D.convert_bullets_in_rect_to_pickups], [method BulletSpawner2D.convert_live_bullets_to_pickups] and [method BulletVolley2D.convert_to_pickups]. A converted bullet appears again where it was, with the look settings (a [SpriteFrames] animation or one texture, size, tint and opacity, fades, material, an attachment, effect layers), moves the way [member motion_mode] says, and is collected when it comes within [member collect_radius] of the target or, with [member collect_on_collision], touches something on its collision mask ([signal BulletFactory2D.pickup_collected], [member collect_callback]).
Look: set [member sprite_frames] (and [member animation]) for an animated coin or gem. The whole pickup volley shows one frame at a time, so every pickup of one conversion animates in sync. [member texture] is only the shortcut for a single static image; with neither, a small white disc is used.
Motion ([member motion_mode]): Burst And Magnet is the built-in coin physics (keeps part of the bullet's velocity, drifts out with drag, then accelerates to the target). Keep Bullet Motion lets every pickup keep the speed, top speed and acceleration its bullet had, and only adds the pull towards the target. Custom hands the speed to your own [member speed_data] and/or [member curves_data] (a speed curve's X axis is the pickup's normalized lifetime). [member rotation_data] spins the pickup in every mode. In all modes the steering towards the target starts after [member magnet_delay_sec].
[codeblock] var frames: SpriteFrames = preload("res://coin_frames.tres") # animations: "spin", "pop"
var coin := BulletPickupData2D.new() coin.sprite_frames = frames coin.animation = &"spin" coin.value = 10 coin.magnet_delay_sec = 0.4 coin.collect_callback = func(target, position, volley, bullet_index, value): score += value
# the boss died: all its bullets become coins and fly to the player boss_spawner.convert_live_bullets_to_pickups(coin, player) # a bomb: everything on screen factory.convert_all_bullets_to_pickups(coin, player) # the same through the signal factory.pickup_collected.connect(func(target, position, volley, bullet_index, value): print(value)) [/codeblock] [signal BulletFactory2D.pickup_collected] works for any Node2D target: an Area2D, a CharacterBody2D, a RigidBody2D, a plain Node2D... With [member collect_on_collision] and a [member collision_mask] the collector is whatever the pickup touches.
Every accepted change emits [signal Resource.changed]; an edit reaches the next conversion, not pickups already flying.

method.name: get_volley_data
method.description: The spawn data of the pickup volley this resource produces (built from the look, motion and collision settings, cached until a property changes). Read it to see exactly what is spawned; changing the returned resource does not change the pickup.

members.member: Which animation of [member sprite_frames] plays. Empty or "default" resolves silently to "default" when it has frames, else to the first animation with frames; an unknown name plays the first animation with frames and pushes one warning. An animation chosen by name that has no frames, or a SpriteFrames without any frames, falls back to [member texture] or the placeholder disc (also one warning). Looping and speed come from the SpriteFrames animation (the bullet rules: [member BulletVolleyData2D.animation]).

A [BulletAttachment2D] scene carried by every pickup (a glow, a sparkle trail, a light). It is pooled and released with the pickup like any bullet attachment and follows [member BulletFactory2D.time_scale] (see [member BulletAttachment2D.apply_time_scale]).
Offset of the attachment from the pickup, in pixels. Must be finite.

Optional [Callable] run for every collected pickup, right after [signal BulletFactory2D.pickup_collected], with the same arguments: [code](target, position, volley, bullet_index, value)[/code]. Runtime only: it is never saved with the resource. An invalid callable is ignored. The bullet is still alive inside the callback.
A sprite effect fired at the pickup's position when it is collected (see [method BulletFactory2D.spawn_layer_effect]).

When on, a pickup is collected by touching something on its [member collision_mask] (an Area2D, a CharacterBody2D, a RigidBody2D, any collision object), and that node is reported as the collector. Needs a collision layer or mask. The touch is consumed: no area/body signal, no bounce. Combined with the radius rule a pickup is still collected exactly once.
A pickup is collected when it comes this close to its target (pixels). Must be finite and above 0.
Played once at the pickup's position when it is collected (see [method BulletFactory2D.play_sound]; its limits and listener rules apply).

Physics layer of the pickup. With a layer or a mask set, the pickup has a small circle area ([member collision_radius]) and the factory's [signal BulletFactory2D.area_entered] / [signal BulletFactory2D.body_entered] work for it, so a player Area2D can touch coins. 0 and 0 (default) means pure distance collection with no physics at all.
Physics layers the pickup detects. See [member collision_layer].
Radius of the pickup's collision circle in pixels, used only with a collision layer or mask. Must be finite and above 0.
Custom motion only: shared [BulletCurvesData2D] of the pickup volley (for example a movement speed curve). The curve's X axis is the pickup's normalized lifetime.
How fast the burst slows down (per second, 1 loses all speed in a second). Applies until the magnet starts. Must be finite and 0 or more.

Sprite effect layers of the pickup volley, exactly like [member BulletVolleyData2D.effect_layers]: a trail that follows the pickup, an On Spawn flash, an On Despawn puff when it leaves the despawn bounds. Collecting a pickup fires none of the hit or destroy layers (use [member collect_effect]).
Seconds the pickup takes to reach full opacity after the conversion. Clamped to the lifetime. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Seconds before expiry over which the pickup fades out (a blinking-out coin). Needs a finite [member lifetime_sec]; clamped to it. Must be finite and 0 or more.
When on, each converted bullet fires its On Clear effects and sounds as it leaves (a bomb flash). Off by default: the bullet just becomes the pickup.

When on and every converted bullet came from volleys of the same spawner, the pickups follow that spawner's [member BulletSpawner2D.time_scale] (while the spawner lives and has [member BulletSpawner2D.time_scale_affects_volleys] on). Off by default: pickups are owned by the factory and run on [member BulletFactory2D.time_scale] only. Conversions that mix spawners ignore the option.
Copies each bullet's custom data resource onto its pickup, readable in [signal BulletFactory2D.pickup_collected] through [method BulletVolley2D.bullet_get_custom_data]. Off by default.
Fraction of the bullet's velocity the pickup keeps for its burst phase (0 stops it dead, 1 keeps the bullet's speed). Must be finite and 0 or more.
How long a pickup lives if nobody collects it. 0 means forever. Must be finite and 0 or more.
How fast the pull accelerates a pickup, in px/s per second, once the magnet runs. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Seconds of burst before the pull to the target begins (steering and acceleration both start then). 0 pulls at once. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Top speed of the pull in px/s (never below the speed the pickup already has). 0 means no top speed (like [member BulletSpeedData2D.max_speed]). Must be finite and 0 or more.

Cap on how fast a pickup may turn towards its target (radians per second per unit; the volley homing smoothing). 0 steers straight at the target at once. A small positive value limits the turning, so pickups swing around in arcs before settling on the target; large values behave like 0. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Material of the pickup volley (an additive glow shader, for example).

How the pickups move: 0 Burst And Magnet (built-in coin physics), 1 Keep Bullet Motion (each pickup keeps its bullet's speed, top speed and acceleration, only the pull is added), 2 Custom (your [member speed_data] / [member curves_data] decide the speed). The knobs a mode does not read are hidden in the inspector. A new mode applies to the next conversion.

When on (default), the factory's despawn bounds remove pickups that fly out of them like any other bullet (a coin that falls off the screen is lost). Turn it off for pickups that must never be culled, for example when the target can be outside the bounds.
Optional [BulletRotationData2D] shared by the pickups: spinning coins. Works in every motion mode and together with the pull towards the target.

With [member rotation_random_min_degrees]: every pickup is turned by a random angle between the two (global random generator). 0 and 0 is off. The pair is not checked against each other; an inverted pair swaps.
Lower end of the random extra rotation. See [member rotation_random_max_degrees].
Multiplies the scale the bullet had when it was converted, so a big bullet can give a bigger coin. Must be finite and above 0.

With [member scale_random_min]: every pickup is additionally scaled by a random factor between the two (global random generator, applied on top of [member scale_multiplier]). 1 and 1 is off. Each must be finite and above 0; an inverted pair swaps.
Lower end of the random scale factor. See [member scale_random_max].
Upper end of the random extra burst speed. See [member scatter_speed_min].

With [member scatter_speed_max]: a random extra burst, each pickup gets a speed between the two in a random direction (Godot's global random generator, so [method @GlobalScope.seed] reproduces it). 0 and 0 is off. The pair is not checked against each other; an inverted pair swaps. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Custom motion only: the [BulletSpeedData2D] (speed, top speed, acceleration) shared by the pickups. Without it a custom pickup has speed 0 and stays where it is until it expires.

The pickup's image and animation: a [SpriteFrames] resource (the animation named by [member animation] plays, its speed and looping come from the resource). Wins over [member texture]. Set this for animated coins and gems. Plain textures or [AtlasTexture] regions of a sprite sheet (drawn as their region, sized as drawn: region plus margin).
Shortcut for a single static image, used only when [member sprite_frames] is empty. With neither, a small white disc is used so a pickup is never invisible.
Drawn size in pixels. (0, 0) uses the size of the texture or of the animation's first frame. Both components must be finite and 0 or more.
Color and opacity of the pickup (alpha is the opacity): a translucent bullet can become a solid gem or the other way round. Every component must be finite.
Anything you want back in [signal BulletFactory2D.pickup_collected]: a number of coins, a dictionary, a resource.
Draw order of the pickup volley (between -4096 and 4096), so coins can sit above or below bullets.

constants.constant: Built-in coin physics: each pickup keeps part of its bullet's velocity, drifts out with drag, and after [member magnet_delay_sec] the magnet accelerates it to the target.
Each pickup keeps the speed, top speed and acceleration of the bullet it was; only the steering towards the target is added.
Your own speed and curves data decide the motion; only the heading comes from the bullet.
